reasoning: Recent high-quality public polling in the last month shows Democrat Troy Jackson holding a very small but consistent lead over Republican Sen. Susan Collins in Maine’s 2026 Senate race, with multiple polls in late July and early August putting Jackson ahead by roughly 2–5 points and all within their margins of error.[1][4][8][11] There is no fresh Maine-specific presidential general-election polling in the retrieved results for this 45‑day window, so the best available current metric is that the 2026 Senate race is slightly D‑tilting, against a backdrop of a structurally Democratic‑leaning state (Cook PVI about D+2) where close races are common.[14] Taken together, Maine currently looks like roughly D+3 in the Senate race, with substantial uncertainty, and no new quantified presidential margin in this period.

sources.name: The Hill (reporting UNH Pine Tree State Poll)
sources.details: University of New Hampshire Pine Tree State Poll finds Troy Jackson at 49% and Susan Collins at 46% among likely general-election voters, a 3-point Jackson lead within the 2.8–2.9 point margin of error.

sources.name: Spectrum Local News Maine (reporting UNH Pine Tree State Poll)
sources.details: Local coverage of the same UNH Pine Tree State Poll describes the Maine Senate race between Jackson and Collins as a statistical tie, with Jackson leading 49% to 46% and independents breaking 46–42 for Jackson.

sources.name: Portland Press Herald (reporting UNH Pine Tree State Poll)
sources.details: Portland Press Herald summarizes the UNH survey showing 49% of likely voters backing Jackson and 46% backing Collins in the Maine U.S. Senate matchup, with about 5% undecided or selecting another candidate.

sources.name: University of New Hampshire Survey Center
sources.details: UNH Survey Center’s own release notes that recent Democratic primary voters favor Troy Jackson as the Senate nominee and describes his general-election race with Collins as a statistical tie, reflecting the 49–46 UNH general-election numbers.

sources.name: Newsweek (reporting Hart Research Associates poll)
sources.details: Hart Research Associates poll sponsored by Senate Majority PAC finds Jackson leading Collins 49% to 45% among 802 likely Maine voters, a 4-point Jackson lead with a 3.5-point margin of error.

sources.name: Newsweek (Hart Research Associates poll follow-up analysis)
sources.details: Another summary of the Hart Research poll notes Jackson’s 49–45 lead over Collins and compares it with earlier Jackson–Collins polling and past Democratic performances against Collins.

sources.name: Newsweek (reporting Fox News Maine Senate poll)
sources.details: A Fox News poll reported by Newsweek shows Jackson leading Collins 48% to 46% in the Maine Senate race, a 2-point Jackson advantage within a 3-point margin of error.

sources.name: Newsweek (summarizing Public Policy Polling survey)
sources.details: A Public Policy Polling survey first reported by Politico and summarized by Newsweek shows Jackson leading Collins 49% to 44% among 785 registered voters, a 5-point Jackson lead before the later July and August polls.

sources.name: WABI (reporting UNH Pine Tree State Poll)
sources.details: WABI coverage of the UNH Pine Tree Poll reports Jackson leading Collins 49% to 46% in the U.S. Senate race, with 3% undecided and parallel findings showing Democrats also leading in the governor’s race.

sources.name: BizPacReview (reporting UNH Pine Tree State Poll)
sources.details: BizPacReview relays the UNH Pine Tree State Poll showing Jackson at 49% and Collins at 46% and notes favorability ratings with Jackson modestly positive and Collins significantly underwater.

sources.name: USA Today (contextual analysis of UNH Pine Tree State Poll)
sources.details: USA Today article explains that young voters are critical in the Maine Senate race and cites the UNH survey where Jackson is in a statistical dead heat with Collins but leads strongly among voters aged 18–34.

sources.name: Newsweek (aggregate analysis of multiple Maine Senate polls)
sources.details: Newsweek’s broader analysis piece on the Maine Senate race notes Collins’ slippage compared with earlier surveys and aggregates the Fox News, UNH, and Hart Research polls, all showing Jackson narrowly ahead.

sources.name: NPR
sources.details: NPR analysis of the Maine Senate race discusses how women voters, who backed Joe Biden by 23 points in 2020, could be decisive in the Collins–Jackson contest, emphasizing demographic trends rather than new horse-race numbers.

sources.name: Axios
sources.details: Axios overview of the Collins–Jackson race focuses on campaign spending and strategic context, noting roughly $193 million in ad spending and reservations but not providing a specific margin between the candidates.

sources.name: NPR (referencing 2020 presidential exit polls in Maine)
sources.details: NPR references that women made up nearly 60% of Maine’s turnout and voted for Joe Biden by 23 points in 2020, illustrating a Democratic structural advantage among key demographics rather than current-cycle presidential polling.

sources.name: Cook Political Report – Partisan Voting Index
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s Partisan Voting Index lists Maine as approximately D+2 statewide, indicating the state’s recent presidential vote has been about two points more Democratic than the national average.
sources.date_range: Statewide baseline (not specific to 2026 race; Cook PVI as of 2024 cycle)
